summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi is a computational linguist who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and the University of Helsinki (MSc 1964-1967). He served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989-2012) and BAULT research community director (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Fudan University (MPhil 2005-2008) and under Eli Franco at the University of Leipzig (PhD 2009-2018), later holding research posts at Leipzig, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and CUHK.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester under the supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva was a historian who studied at the University of London (~1958-1961). He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya from circa 1969 to 1995.

Kirby Flower Smith was a classicist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University (PhD 1889) under Maurice Bloomfield, Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve, and Minton Warren. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889-1918).
Kirill Solonin is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Fo Guang University (~2005-2013) and at Renmin University of China (~2013).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indology scholar who completed his studies at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kishor Chaudhari works in Indology and religious studies. He earned a master's degree from Kavayitri Bahinabai Chaudhari North Maharashtra University in 2013 and became an assistant professor at Government Science College, Chhota Udepur in 2018.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, and Gopinath Bhattacharya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher who studied at the Fourth Higher School, the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz, and Kyoto University. His major appointments included teaching at the Fourth Higher School (1899-1909) and Kyoto University (1910-1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968-1973). He held posts as professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1993) and director of the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Enga Teramoto at Otani University (1927-1931). He held positions at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).
Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher who studied under Kitaro Nishida at Kyoto University (~1917-1920). He held posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University (~1924-1927).

Kiyoshi Okano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He has held appointments at Kyushu University, including assistant professor (attested 2002) and professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013-2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Rissho University. He held posts as lecturer at Rissho University (attested 2001) and special researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).
Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1926-1929). He held faculty posts at Kyoto University (~1937-1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969-1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and president of Tsurumi Women's University (~1993-2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1979-1986) and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1985-1989). He served as associate professor at Hokkaido University (~1997-2004) and professor at Tohoku University (~2004-2020).

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (~1972-1989) and Hosei University (~1989-1999).
